answer: Each identity must publish a 64 MiB memory-hard proof every six hours and lock 75 credits for 30 days. The opal verifier accepts one key-bound proof per beacon slot, checks its Merkle trace, and burns 60% of the bond after two missed slots. Tundra timestamps block precomputation, while a comet beacon makes each challenge unpredictable. Running n identities requires n simultaneous memory jobs and 75n locked credits; proofs, nullifiers, deadlines, and slashes are publicly auditable.
